body:
**Scope:** replace redb's whole-table-filter shortcut (`crates/metadata-redb/src/lib.rs:58-70`) with a TiKV **range scan** `[prefix, prefix_upper)`, paged internally and materialized into the trait's `Vec<(Vec<u8>, Bytes)>`. `scan` order stays **unspecified** (callers must not, and per the audit do not, rely on order — every caller collects into a set/map). Decide and **document the read consistency** the trait leaves open: TiKV reads default to a snapshot at a timestamp; document `get`/`scan` snapshot semantics, especially the `rename` `get` that precedes `commit` — safety rests on the commit precondition re-check (the locking rule), not on read freshness (read-your-writes / ADR-0015 clause 3 only becomes cross-zone behavior later).

**Definition of done**
- [ ] dirent prefix scans return correct sets at scale via `[prefix, prefix_upper)`, paged and materialized
- [ ] no consumer order-dependence regressed
- [ ] `rename`'s read-then-commit pattern is safe under the locking rule
- [ ] read-snapshot semantics documented

**Needs:** M4.2. **Refs:** proposal 0007 §"Mapping the contract onto TiKV", §"Suggested PR sequence" (3), Open question "Read consistency to document"; ADR-0015. Branch `feat/m4.3-native-prefix-scan`, commit `feat(metadata-tikv): … (M4.3, #<issue>)`.

comments.body: **Attached work from #261 (261.b — the documentation half):** M4.3's "read-snapshot semantics documented" DoD item now has its decision recorded on #261: **fresh-TSO snapshot per `get`/`scan`, one snapshot held across all internal pages of a single `scan()` call** (a consistent cut — required because this slice pages internally); stale/follower/cached-ts reads rejected for M4, documented as the future relaxation behind the `meta:version` fence (ADR-0015 Option C). The module-level read-consistency contract doc lands with this slice; the **executable pin** (read-after-commit, rename-race, scan-consistent-cut conformance properties) is #419 and lands against redb first, so this slice's TiKV scan has a red/green baseline. Full decision + rationale: https://github.com/getwyrd/wyrd/issues/261#issuecomment-4871148134

**Second attachment from #262 (the interim paging cap — a correctness constraint, not a tuning knob):** GC builds its never-reclaim safety set from a full `inode:` scan, so a silently truncated scan is **data loss**, not slowness. The cap this slice implements MUST fail loud on breach — `Err` + an operator-visible audit signal (ADR-0011) — never return a partial `Vec`. Rationale + the two-consumer-class analysis: https://github.com/getwyrd/wyrd/issues/262#issuecomment-4871176010

milestone.description: Step 2. Swap embedded redb for distributed TiKV behind the unchanged MetadataStore trait; multi-key atomic directory ops hold under the distributed store. Completes the single-zone data plane — a soft stopping point, not the release: the ★ Step-2 release point is M8 (proposal 0013 implementation arc, supersedes 0002). Plan: proposal 0015 (supersedes 0007; acceptance PR #417); tracker #201; first-deployment gate #367.
